title: Static browser journey harness
description:
Objective: stand up the browser driver, its config, a distinct script, and a served static bundle, with one smoke journey proving the harness works. This is the half of the journey-gate harness that is buildable TODAY, with no daemon.

WHY THIS EXISTS. task-3f503779a29c4e4c9a61db6520715609 was authored as a single harness task whose DoD bundled the browser driver together with "drives it against a real daemon process". A planning probe found the daemon half unbuildable: there is NO HTTP listener anywhere in the repo (grep for createServer(, .listen(, Deno.serve, Bun.serve across apps, packages and adapters returns ZERO), apps/daemon/package.json declares no main and no bin so it is not a startable process, packages/control-room-client exports only createCompatGate plus types with zero transport, and apps/control-room imports that client with "import type" only. That task is now BLOCKED and holds the daemon-connected composition; this task holds the part that works.

WHAT IS BUILDABLE TODAY, verified: apps/control-room builds with vite build and dist/ already contains index.html plus assets. index.html mounts /src/main.tsx, and main.tsx mounts ControlRoomScaffold, which renders committed fixture surfaces. So the app is fully renderable standalone — it simply is not daemon-connected.

WHAT IS ABSENT, verified: grep for playwright|puppeteer|cypress|selenium|webdriver across EVERY package.json (root, apps/*, packages/*) returns ZERO. No browser config exists at any depth. tests/e2e/control-room/ does not exist; tests/e2e contains only foundation/. The existing "pnpm test:e2e" is Vitest under Node — package.json:18 is `tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json && vitest run tests/e2e` — and must not be absorbed or retargeted.

NOT IN SCOPE: anything requiring a daemon; the J1-J6 scenarios; the twenty-case matrix; contrast certification; the p95/p99 run. Those belong to task-667b1085 and task-3f503779. Ship the harness and exactly one smoke journey — nothing that reads like a product certification.

Owned paths: tests/e2e/control-room/**, the browser driver config, and the root package.json script entry.

Hard dependencies: none.

Verification: the new browser script exits 0, and pnpm test:e2e still exits 0 unchanged.
definitionOfDone: A browser driver is declared as a devDependency with an exact pinned version (the repo sets saveExact: true) plus a committed config, and the task records in one sentence which driver was chosen and why. The repo declares none today — grep for playwright|puppeteer|cypress|selenium|webdriver across every package.json returns zero.
A NEW script drives the browser, separate from test:e2e. test:e2e must keep its exact current definition and still exit 0 — the Node foundation lane is not absorbed, retargeted or widened.

The harness serves the real built static bundle from apps/control-room (vite build output, or vite preview) and tears the server down on EVERY exit path including failure. A leaked process or port is a defect: on Windows a surviving child holds file handles and surfaces later as EBUSY rather than the real error.

Exactly ONE smoke journey ships: load the served page, assert the committed test id cr.shell.root is present, exit. It asserts the element was actually found rather than that no error was thrown. It must NOT assert any J1-J6 acceptance criterion, contrast, layout, or timing — a smoke test wearing a journey's name would retire an obligation it did not discharge.

Build, serve, readiness and teardown failures each return a distinct stable reason code and a test asserts the specific code, not merely that the run failed. Follow the existing E2E_* convention in tests/e2e/foundation/e2e-harness.ts (E2E_CLEANUP_FAILED, E2E_PROCESS_ALREADY_KILLED, E2E_UNDECLARED_BOUNDARY, E2E_UNKNOWN_KILL_TARGET) WITHOUT importing that module.
Readiness is awaited by polling the served URL until it answers, never by a fixed sleep, and the wait has a bounded timeout that fails with its own reason code.

The harness records honestly, in the task and in a comment on task-3f503779, that this journey runs against FIXTURE-BACKED UI with no daemon attached, so nobody later mistakes a green smoke run for a connected-system proof.
taskRails: Do NOT reuse or extend tests/e2e/foundation/**. Its own header states: 'This module is NOT part of the system under certification and must never stand in for one.' Its real-process termination in e2e-process.ts is deliberately fenced to that directory — do not import it and do not widen the fence.

Never imply a daemon was involved. The served app renders committed fixtures via ControlRoomScaffold; there is no transport in the repo. Any artifact, log line, or test name suggesting a connected system is a fabricated certification and is forbidden by epic rail 4.
Ship the harness and one smoke journey only. Any scenario resembling a J1-J6 acceptance case belongs to task-667b1085.
A browser driver pulls a large dependency tree and a binary download. Pin the version exactly and state whether CI must download browsers, so the gate is reproducible rather than machine-dependent.
Preserve foreign work; stage and commit only explicit owned paths. Never git add -A. Keep each file below 400 lines, target 250.

implementationPlan.description: Establish the lane separation before writing anything, because getting it wrong breaks DoD 2 silently. Read the ROOT vitest.config.ts and confirm include is ["packages/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.ts"] with environment "node". Read root package.json:18 and confirm test:e2e is `tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json && vitest run tests/e2e`. Conclude and write down the rule this plan depends on: browser specs MUST be named *.spec.ts so the root include cannot sweep them into the Node lane, while a pure-logic *.test.ts in the same directory is deliberately allowed and will run in that lane. Read tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json and note include ["./*.ts"] scopes the existing tsc leg to that directory only. Read tests/e2e/foundation/e2e-harness.ts for the E2E_* stable-code and cleanup-in-finally conventions to MIRROR — importing anything from that subtree is forbidden by task rail 2 and by its own header. Record the current `pnpm test:e2e` exit code and the list of files it runs; that is the baseline DoD 2 is measured against. No files are modified.
implementationPlan.note:
Lane separation established by reading the config, not by assuming it. No files modified.

MEASURED
- Root `vitest.config.ts`: `environment: "node"`, `include: ["packages/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.ts"]`, `passWithNoTests: false`, `sequence.concurrent: false`. Verbatim, as the plan predicted.
- Root `package.json:18`: `"test:e2e": "tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json && vitest run tests/e2e"`. Unchanged.
- `tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json` has `include: ["./*.ts"]` — directory-scoped, so the existing `tsc -p` leg will NOT typecheck a new sibling directory. And `pnpm typecheck` is `pnpm --recursive typecheck` over workspace packages; `tests/` is not one. **So nothing typechecks `tests/e2e/control-room/` unless step 4 adds a sibling tsconfig.** That is a real gap, not a formality.
- `tests/e2e/` contains only `foundation/`: `e2e-harness.{ts,test.ts}`, `e2e-process.ts`, `foundation-fixtures.ts`, `journey-spec.ts`, `release-manifest.{ts,test.ts}`, `tsconfig.json`.

THE RULE THIS PLAN DEPENDS ON, now confirmed rather than inherited:
**Browser specs MUST be `*.spec.ts`.** The root include matches `tests/**/*.test.ts` only, so `*.spec.ts` is invisible to the Node lane and the two lanes are disjoint BY NAMING with zero config surgery. The converse is deliberate and useful: a pure-logic `*.test.ts` in the same directory IS swept into the Node lane, which is exactly where step 2's stable-code tests belong — proven without paying for a browser.
The failure mode if this is got wrong is silent: a browser spec named `*.test.ts` would be executed by `vitest run tests/e2e` under Node with no browser, and `passWithNoTests: false` would not save it. Step 7 must prove it in BOTH directions.

BASELINE FOR DoD 2, captured before any edit: `pnpm test:e2e` -> **exit 0, 2 files / 34 tests**. The two files are `foundation/e2e-harness.test.ts` and `foundation/release-manifest.test.ts`. Step 7 compares against exactly this: same exit code, same two files, and no `*.spec.ts` in the output.

CONVENTION TO MIRROR WITHOUT IMPORTING (task rail 2, and that file's own header forbids standing in for it): `e2e-harness.ts:30` exports a FROZEN tuple `E2E_ERROR_CODES = ["E2E_CLEANUP_FAILED", "E2E_PROCESS_ALREADY_KILLED", "E2E_UNDECLARED_BOUNDARY", "E2E_UNKNOWN_KILL_TARGET"]` with `type E2eErrorCode = (typeof ...)[number]`; cleanup runs in a `finally` (:208); a throwing cleanup does not prevent the rest, and the outcome carries `{ok: false, code: "E2E_CLEANUP_FAILED", failures}` naming WHICH failed (:184). I will mirror the shape — frozen tuple, derived union, cleanup-in-finally, outcome names the failing cleanup — with my own distinct codes for build/bind/readiness/cleanup, and import nothing from that subtree.

Worth flagging from its header for whoever reviews: that module's determinism scan is TEXT-EXACT over the raw source and its own header deliberately avoids naming the four forbidden APIs literally, so it cannot be fooled by a parser edge case. My directory is outside that scan; I should not assume its guarantees extend here.

NEXT RISK I AM CARRYING INTO STEP 4, stated now rather than discovered late: the driver install pulls a browser BINARY that lives outside the pnpm lockfile. If that download is unavailable in this environment, the harness code is still writable and testable in the Node lane (step 2/3 use injected fakes and start no real process), but the browser lane itself cannot be proven green here. That would be a disclosed environment limitation, not a fabricated pass — I will measure it at step 4 and say so plainly rather than reporting a green I did not observe.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red in the Node lane: write the failing spec for the harness lifecycle's stable reason codes, as a *.test.ts so it runs inside the existing test:e2e without a browser. Cover one distinct, specific code per failure: the build step fails; the server fails to bind; readiness is never reached within the bounded timeout; teardown fails. Assert the exact code in each case, never merely that the run failed. Drive every case with injected fakes for spawn and probe — this test must NOT start a real server or a real build; that is the browser lane's job. Assert cleanup runs on every exit path including when the body throws, that a throwing cleanup does not prevent the remaining cleanups, and that the outcome names WHICH cleanup failed, mirroring the foundation harness's guarantee without importing it. Tests fail because the harness does not exist.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED. `pnpm exec vitest run tests/e2e/control-room` -> exit 1, `Tests no tests`, module-load failure on `./harness.js`. The harness does not exist, which is the expected failure.

That `no tests` shape is the right red HERE — a missing module cannot be imported, so nothing runs — but it is the same output a broken-syntax mutation produces, so I am naming the distinction rather than relying on it: for the step-8 drills, a real red must show a NAMED failing case with the other cases still passing.

Named `harness.test.ts`, NOT `.spec.ts`, deliberately: the root include is `tests/**/*.test.ts`, so this runs in the existing Node lane inside `pnpm test:e2e` with no browser and no real process. That is the correct home for lifecycle logic — a test that needed a real server could not assert the readiness-timeout path without actually waiting for it.

TWELVE CASES, every one driving INJECTED ports; nothing here builds a bundle, binds a port or launches a browser.
- Vocabulary: exactly four frozen codes in order.
- One distinct code per failure, each asserted specifically: `E2E_BUNDLE_BUILD_FAILED` (and the server is proven never reached), `E2E_SERVER_BIND_FAILED` for both a null return AND a throw (and the probe is proven never reached), `E2E_READINESS_TIMEOUT` under an advancing injected clock.
- The readiness cases are asserted in BOTH directions: the timeout case asserts it actually polled (`polls > 0`) before giving up — a wait that never polled would satisfy the code assertion while proving nothing — and the success case asserts it stopped at the third poll rather than waiting out the budget.
- Cleanup on every exit path: server stopped when the body succeeds, stopped when the body THROWS, `E2E_CLEANUP_FAILED` naming WHICH cleanup failed (`failures: ["server"]`), and — the one most likely to be got wrong — a cleanup failure does NOT overwrite the body's primary code, since the operator needs the reason the run failed at all.

Time is an injected `now()`, never a real clock or a sleep; the timeout cases terminate because the injected clock advances, not because anything waited.

Imports nothing from `tests/e2e/foundation/**` — task rail 2 and that module's own header. The conventions are MIRRORED: frozen tuple, cleanup in finally, outcome names the failing cleanup.

implementationPlan.description: Make step 2 green. Implement the harness lifecycle: build or reuse the apps/control-room bundle, serve it on an EPHEMERAL port, poll the served URL until it answers with a bounded timeout, hand the resolved base URL to the caller, and tear the server down in a finally on every exit path. Export a frozen tuple of stable reason codes mirroring the foundation convention (build, bind, readiness, cleanup), and return them rather than throwing bare errors. Take spawn and probe as injected dependencies so step 2's tests can drive every branch without real processes. Poll for readiness; never sleep a fixed duration. Keep the module under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm exec vitest run tests/e2e/control-room` -> exit 0, **10/10**. `pnpm test:e2e` -> exit 0, 3 files / 44 tests.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN STEP-2 NOTE: I wrote "twelve cases". It is **ten**. Counted, not estimated.

DoD 2 — READ THIS CAREFULLY, because the number moved and it is not what step 7 must flag.
`test:e2e` went from **2 files / 34 tests** to **3 files / 44 tests**. Its DEFINITION is byte-unchanged (`tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json && vitest run tests/e2e`) and it still exits 0. The third file is my own `harness.test.ts`, which the plan explicitly sanctions running in that lane. The Node foundation lane is not absorbed, retargeted or widened — foundation's two files still run, unchanged, and I edited nothing under `tests/e2e/foundation/`.
So step 7's real obligation is narrower than "the file set is unchanged": **no `*.spec.ts` may appear in that output.** I am restating it because my own step-1 note phrased the baseline as "the same two files", and that phrasing would now read as a violation of something nobody actually requires.

TWO DESIGN DECISIONS I CHANGED WHILE IMPLEMENTING, both worth reviewing.
1. **A failing journey assertion now PROPAGATES; it is not laundered into a reason code.** My step-2 test originally expected a throwing body to come back as `{ok:false}`. That was wrong: harness failures are the harness's to name, but a smoke assertion that failed is the CALLER's failure and must fail as itself — swallowing it into a harness code would let a broken journey read like a tidy infrastructure refusal. The server still comes down first, and the test now asserts both: `rejects.toThrow("assertion failed")` AND `stopped === 1`.
2. Dropped a `bodyFailed` flag that would have forced me to reuse `E2E_READINESS_TIMEOUT` as the code for a body failure. Reusing a code that describes a different failure is exactly the "assertion detached from its subject" defect the epic rail names.

ALSO FIXED BEFORE IT SHIPPED: my first draft declared the cleanup result with `var` inside the `finally` and read it afterwards, relying on hoisting. It works and it is indefensible; now a `let` declared before the `try`.

LIFECYCLE PROPERTIES, all pinned by the ten cases: build refuses before the server starts; bind refuses before the probe runs (both a null return and a throw); readiness POLLS with a bounded 30s budget against an INJECTED clock and never sleeps; cleanup runs in a `finally` on every exit path; a failing cleanup names WHICH one (`failures: ["server"]`); and a cleanup failure never overwrites an earlier code.

One subtlety in `awaitReadiness` worth naming: the deadline is checked AFTER each probe rather than only between fast polls, so a probe that itself resolves slowly still terminates. A loop that only checked between polls would spin forever against a slow probe — green in the fake, hanging in reality.

Imports nothing from `tests/e2e/foundation/**`. Module is 150 lines.

STATUS FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: steps 4-9 remain, and step 4 is the risk — it installs a browser driver whose binaries live outside the pnpm lockfile. Steps 2 and 3 were built to be independent of that on purpose: the lifecycle is fully proven in the Node lane with injected ports, so if the binary download is unavailable in this environment the harness logic is still verified and only the browser lane is unprovable. That would be a disclosed environment limitation, never a fabricated green.

implementationPlan.description: Add the browser driver and its config. Declare the driver as a devDependency with an EXACT pinned version — pnpm-workspace.yaml sets saveExact true and engineStrict true, and root engines pin node >=24.16.0 <25 with pnpm 11.0.8, so a caret range is a violation. Add the config with testDir pointing at this directory and testMatch restricted to *.spec.ts, so the browser lane and the Node lane stay disjoint by naming. Restrict the smoke lane to ONE browser to keep the gate cheap and reproducible. Record in the task, in one sentence, which driver was chosen and why, and state explicitly whether CI must run a browser-binary install step — those binaries live outside the pnpm lockfile and an unstated binary dependency is how a gate becomes machine-dependent. Add a sibling tsconfig for this directory: the existing `tsc -p` leg covers only tests/e2e/foundation, and `pnpm typecheck` is recursive over workspace packages, which tests/ is not.
implementationPlan.note:
Driver landed, pinned, typechecked. `pnpm exec tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` -> exit 0.

DRIVER CHOICE, one sentence as DoD 1 requires: **@playwright/test 1.62.1**, chosen because its default `testMatch` is `*.spec.ts`, which is exactly the naming the root vitest `include` (`tests/**/*.test.ts`) cannot see — so the browser lane and the Node lane stay disjoint by naming with zero config surgery on `test:e2e`, and it ships runner + config + assertions as ONE pinned package rather than a driver plus a separate runner.

CI BINARY REQUIREMENT — STATED, NOT ASSUMED (task rail 5). **CI MUST run `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` before the browser script.** Measured here: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ms-playwright` did not exist before this step; after the install it holds `chromium-1234`, `chromium_headless_shell-1234`, `ffmpeg-1011`, `winldd-1007` — 114.5 MiB downloaded from cdn.playwright.dev. Those bytes are NOT in pnpm-lock.yaml and `pnpm install` alone will not produce them. Without that step the lane fails on a missing executable, not on a real defect.

VERSION PIN. `"@playwright/test": "1.62.1"` — bare, no caret. pnpm-workspace.yaml sets `saveExact: true` and `engineStrict: true`, so a range would be a violation. Edited root package.json BY HAND (one line inserted before `@types/node`) rather than via `pnpm add`, precisely because task-1cafc7f9 is concurrently WORKING in that file and `pnpm add` rewrites/reorders the whole manifest. `pnpm install` -> exit 0, `+ @playwright/test 1.62.1`, 3 packages added. The one new SCRIPT is deliberately still absent; that is step 6.

FILES ADDED (all inside owned paths)
- `tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts` — `testDir: "."`, `testMatch: "*.spec.ts"`, ONE project (chromium), `workers: 1`, `retries: 0`, `forbidOnly: true`, `reporter: [["list"]]`.
- `tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` — sibling, `include: ["./*.ts"]`. Needed because the existing `tsc -p` leg is scoped to `tests/e2e/foundation` by its own `include: ["./*.ts"]`, and `pnpm typecheck` is `pnpm --recursive typecheck` over workspace packages (`apps/*`, `adapters/*`, `packages/*`) — `tests/` is not one, so nothing typechecked this directory at all.
- `tests/e2e/control-room/.gitignore` — `test-results/`, `playwright-report/`.

THREE DECISIONS WORTH THE NEXT AGENT'S ATTENTION

1. **No `webServer` block.** Playwright's built-in serve/readiness would report Playwright's messages, and DoD 5 demands a distinct stable code per failure asserted specifically. The lifecycle stays ours (`harness.ts`), driven from inside the journey. This was approach (2) in planningNotes and is rejected as the primary mechanism, not merely unused.

2. **`browserName: "chromium"` directly, NOT `...devices["Desktop Chrome"]`.** The generated-config idiom pulls a device descriptor whose channel handling can reach for an installed Google Chrome; a gate that silently depends on a browser the install step did not place is the machine-dependence rail 5 exists to prevent. One explicit browser, no emulation.

3. **`lib: ["ES2024", "DOM"]` in the new tsconfig.** `tsconfig.base.json` is `lib: ["ES2024"]` only, and playwright-core's `types.d.ts` then fails with 40+ `TS2304: Cannot find name 'HTMLElement' / 'SVGElement'`. That is a real requirement of driving a browser, not a workaround — but note the side effect: `harness.test.ts` in this same directory now also sees DOM globals, so a Node-vs-DOM mix-up (`setTimeout` returning `number` vs `Timeout`) would no longer be caught by the typechecker here.

`forbidOnly: true` is unconditional rather than CI-gated: with exactly one smoke journey, a stray `.only` would shrink the lane to nothing while still exiting 0. Not yet proven that the empty lane fails — Playwright's `--pass-with-no-tests` defaults off, but step 7 must MEASURE that rather than trust it, since "0 tests reported as success" is the exact silent failure the plan names.

implementationPlan.description: Write the ONE smoke journey as a *.spec.ts. It loads the served page via the harness's base URL and asserts the committed test id cr.shell.root is PRESENT — assert the element was actually found, not that no error was thrown, since a page that failed to mount throws nothing. That is the entire journey. It must NOT assert any J1-J6 acceptance criterion, any truth-class or provenance behaviour, contrast, layout, or timing: those belong to task-667b1085, and a smoke test wearing a journey's name would retire an obligation it did not discharge. Name the file and the test so that neither implies a certification or a connected system.
implementationPlan.note:
ONE smoke journey, GREEN against a real Chromium. `pnpm exec playwright test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts` -> exit 0, `ok 1 [chromium] > ... serving the built control-room bundle mounts its shell root element (776ms)`, `1 passed`. `tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` -> exit 0.

THE STEP NEEDED A FILE THE PLAN DID NOT NAME, and this is the honest part to read. `harness.ts` is PURE — every effect is an injected port, which is what made the reason codes provable in the Node lane. Nothing in the repo supplied the REAL ports. So `static-ports.ts` (168 lines, inside owned paths) now holds the actual `vite build`, the actual static server and the actual HTTP probe. Without it the spec would have had to reimplement the lifecycle inline, which is the "authority reimplemented inside the test" defect.

ASSERTION SHAPE, because DoD 4 turns on it. Two assertions, both non-vacuous:
- `await expect(shellRoot).toHaveCount(1)` inside the body — asserts the element was FOUND, and auto-retries while the module script executes. A page that fails to mount throws nothing, so "no error was thrown" would have proven nothing.
- `expect(outcome).toEqual({ ok: true, value: 1 })` outside — pins the HARNESS outcome as well, so a run that refused with a reason code, or never reached the body at all, cannot read as a pass.
Scope held: no J1-J6 criterion, no truth-class or provenance behaviour, no contrast, no layout, no timing. Neither the file name (`control-room-smoke.spec.ts`) nor the test name says journey, certified or connected.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: THE BUILD REALLY RUNS. 776ms for the whole test looked too fast for a build, so I checked instead of believing it. `apps/control-room/dist/index.html` mtime moved to 17:31:51 DURING the playwright run, and a standalone `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room build` is `real 0m0.637s` exit 0. Vite 8 is genuinely that fast here. The bundle served is freshly built, not a stale `dist/` — which also means a broken source reddens this lane rather than being masked.

FIVE DECISIONS IN static-ports.ts
1. **buildBundle fails closed twice**: non-zero exit AND a missing `dist/index.html` afterwards. The second catches `REPO_ROOT` resolved by hop count (`resolve(HERE, "..", "..", "..")`) against a directory that later moved — the failure mode where every assertion still passes over a smaller set.
2. **No SPA fallback.** Rewriting a miss to index.html would answer 200 for a missing asset, so a bundle with a broken script tag would still serve a blank page that probes ready.
3. **Explicit content-type map.** A module served as `application/octet-stream` is refused by the browser and the app silently never mounts — that failure would surface as "element missing", pointing at the wrong thing.
4. **Teardown calls `closeAllConnections()`, not just `close()`.** `close()` waits for keep-alive sockets a just-loaded page still holds; on Windows the survivor keeps file handles and resurfaces later as EBUSY.
5. **Traversal guard** on the resolved path, and an ephemeral port (`listen(0, "127.0.0.1")`) so parallel runs cannot collide.

TWO SMALL CORRECTIONS MADE MID-STEP
- First run emitted `DEP0190 DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true`. Node needs `shell: true` for `pnpm` (.cmd) but deprecates the argv-array form with it. Now ONE fixed command string; warning gone, nothing interpolated.
- Added `timeout: 180_000` to playwright.config.ts. The default 30s is not the right budget for a lane that builds before serving. Still bounded, and the harness's own `READINESS_BUDGET_MS` refuses with `E2E_READINESS_TIMEOUT` well inside it.

FILE SIZES (rail 5, per file): spec 30, harness.test.ts 211, harness.ts 152, playwright.config.ts 43, static-ports.ts 168. All under 250.

NOT YET PROVEN, and step 7 must MEASURE both rather than trust them: that `pnpm test:e2e` still exits 0 with no `*.spec.ts` in its output, and that an EMPTY browser lane fails rather than reporting 0 tests as success.

implementationPlan.note:
Contended file edited safely. `pnpm test:e2e:browser` -> exit 0, `1 passed`.

THE SCRIPT
`"test:e2e:browser": "tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json && playwright test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts"`
Deliberately mirrors `test:e2e`'s two-leg shape (typecheck leg, then run leg) so the typecheck cannot be skipped by running the driver directly. Placed on the line AFTER `test:e2e` — adjacent to the lane it must stay disjoint from, so a future reader sees both at once.

CONTENTION HANDLED, NOT ASSUMED AWAY. Re-read root package.json immediately before writing; it was byte-identical to my step-4 state, so task-1cafc7f9 had not landed anything in the window. Used a targeted Edit, never a whole-file write, never `pnpm add` (which reorders the manifest). `git diff -- package.json` is exactly TWO added lines and zero modified lines: the `@playwright/test` devDependency and the one script. `test:e2e` is byte-unchanged.

REQUIRED CO-CHANGE DISCLOSED: pnpm-lock.yaml. Adding a devDependency without updating the lockfile leaves the repo unable to reproduce the install, so the lock is committed with it. Audited rather than trusted: `git diff -- pnpm-lock.yaml` is +38/-0, and every added line is attributable to playwright — the specifier/version pair, playwright-core, and `fsevents@2.3.2` which is an optional `os: [darwin]` transitive. Nothing foreign rode along.

COMMITTED BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC as `cc68056`, 7 files, 298 insertions, 0 deletions: package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, and the five files under tests/e2e/control-room/. No `git add -A`. Committing now rather than at the end is deliberate for TWO reasons — foreign whole-tree completion hooks have swept in-progress files four times today, and step 8's mutation drills need a clean restore point so a drill edit cannot be captured by someone else's sweep and then silently persist.

STILL OUTSTANDING, and step 7 must MEASURE both directions rather than infer either: `pnpm test:e2e` unchanged in exit code with NO `*.spec.ts` in its output, and an empty browser lane FAILING rather than reporting zero tests as success.

QA FULL VERIFICATION RECORD (approval summary capped at 2000 chars).

BOTH LANES RE-RUN BY ME, the DoD's own command:
- `pnpm test:e2e` -> exit 0, 3 files / 44 tests. The Node lane still passes, unabsorbed.
- `pnpm test:e2e:browser` -> exit 0, `ok 1 [chromium] control-room-smoke.spec.ts:17 serving the built control-room bundle mounts its shell root element`. A real chromium run, not a stub.

DoD 1 — MET. `@playwright/test` at `1.62.1`, **exact, no range prefix**, so the repo's saveExact discipline holds. Config committed at `tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts`. The choice and its CI consequence are recorded in the commit message: *"CI must run `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` before this script; the browser binaries are not in pnpm-lock.yaml."* That is rail 5's reproducibility clause answered in the place a future operator will actually hit it.

DoD 2 — MET, and the mechanism is structural rather than conventional, which is what makes it hold. `git show cc68056 -- package.json` is **2 insertions, 0 deletions, 0 modified lines**: the devDependency and the new script. `test:e2e` is byte-identical. Crucially, the two lanes are disjoint **by file naming against the root vitest config**: `include: ["packages/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.ts"]`, and the browser journey is `*.spec.ts`. So `test:e2e` structurally *cannot* pick up a browser spec — it is not a convention someone must remember. Directory holds exactly `control-room-smoke.spec.ts` and `harness.test.ts`; no browser spec named `*.test.ts`, no Node test named `*.spec.ts`.

DoD 3 — MET. Teardown is in a `finally` and runs on every path including a throwing body. Two details worth naming because both are the difference between a real teardown and one that looks right: `closeAllConnections()` is called alongside `close()`, because `close()` alone waits out the keep-alive socket a just-loaded page holds — that is precisely the Windows leak the DoD warns surfaces later as EBUSY rather than the real error; and the port is ephemeral, so parallel runs cannot collide. Covered by the Node-lane case "stops the server when the body THROWS, and lets the failure propagate".

DoD 4 — MET, and this is the item most at risk of quiet overreach. Exactly ONE `test()` call in one spec file. It asserts `toHaveCount(1)` on `cr.shell.root` — the element was **found**, with Playwright's retry covering the module script — and then pins the harness outcome to `{ ok: true, value: 1 }`, so a run that never reached the body, or refused with a reason code, cannot read as a pass. Its header explicitly disclaims J1-J6, truth-class and provenance behaviour, contrast, layout and timing, and names task-667b1085 as their owner. The file name, the test name and the commit message all avoid "journey", "gate" and "certified".

DoD 5 — MET. Four frozen codes defined LOCALLY — `E2E_BUNDLE_BUILD_FAILED`, `E2E_SERVER_BIND_FAILED`, `E2E_READINESS_TIMEOUT`, `E2E_CLEANUP_FAILED` — with a vocabulary test asserting exactly those four and `Object.isFrozen`. Every one has a test asserting **that specific code**, not merely that the run failed, including both arms of bind failure (server returns null, and startServer throws). Precedence is explicit and tested: build refuses before the server starts, bind refuses before the probe runs, and a cleanup failure never overwrites an earlier code — "keeps the body's failure code when cleanup ALSO fails".

DoD 6 — MET, and tested in BOTH directions, which is what makes it more than a timeout. `awaitReadiness` polls with `POLL_INTERVAL_MS` between attempts and a bounded `READINESS_BUDGET_MS`; "refuses E2E_READINESS_TIMEOUT rather than polling forever" covers the failure arm, and "succeeds as soon as the probe answers, without waiting out the budget" covers the success arm — without the second, a harness that always slept the full budget would pass. No `page.waitForTimeout` anywhere; the single `setTimeout` is the poll interval, i.e. the loop's yield, not a wait-and-assume.

DoD 7 — MET, with a judgement call I checked rather than accepted. The DoD names a comment on **task-3f503779**; that task is **ARCHIVED as superseded**. The worker posted the disclosure on **task-667b1085** (Control-room journey gate, BLOCKED — the live successor) and stated why in the comment itself: *"Posting here rather than on task-3f503779, which is ARCHIVED as superseded."* I verified both: 3f503779 has zero comments and is archived; 667b1085 carries the disclosure, headed **"THE NEW BROWSER LANE RUNS AGAINST FIXTURE-BACKED UI WITH NO DAEMON ATTACHED."** That serves DoD 7's stated purpose — *"so nobody later mistakes a green smoke run for a connected-system proof"* — better than the literal target would, since a warning on an archived task is a warning nobody reads. Substituted openly, not silently.

RAIL 2 — HONOURED. `grep -rn foundation tests/e2e/control-room/` returns exactly two hits, **both inside doc comments** naming the convention being mirrored. Zero import statements, so the fenced real-process termination in `e2e-process.ts` is neither imported nor widened.

RAIL 3 — HONOURED. Every occurrence of daemon/connected/certified in the new files is a disclaimer stating the opposite.

planningNotes.risks:
1. ROOT package.json IS CONTENDED RIGHT NOW. task-1cafc7f9fcdc4c9299860b6b1e38275d (Doctor exact runtime and tool version reporting) is WORKING and also owns root package.json, and governor-f70d1157's promotion note warns that four completion-hook sweeps have captured foreign in-progress files today. DoD 2 requires test:e2e to still exit 0, so prove it: run test:e2e AFTER adding the browser files and confirm it is unchanged in both exit code and the set of files it ran.

Pin the package version exactly per saveExact, restrict to ONE browser for the smoke lane, and state in the task whether CI must run an install step — an unstated binary dependency is the classic "works on my machine" gate.

5. LEAKED SERVERS AND PORTS. Use an ephemeral port so parallel runs cannot collide, and tear down on EVERY exit path including a thrown assertion. On Windows a surviving child holds file handles and surfaces later as EBUSY rather than the real error.

6. READINESS BY POLLING, NEVER A FIXED SLEEP, with a bounded timeout that fails with its own code. A sleep long enough to be reliable is long enough to make the gate annoying, and a sleep short enough to be fast is flaky.

7. DO NOT let this grow into the journey gate. Exactly one smoke journey. Anything resembling a J1-J6 case belongs to task-667b1085.
